channel.title: ManufacturingDive – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from ManufacturingDive – Bias and Credibility (manufacturingdive.com)

item.title: Toyota suppliers seek relief from USMCA review
item.description: The automaker’s executives said they want federal officials to keep the agreement trilateral, as the company has supply chains and 14 manufacturing plants across North America.

item.title: AI boom drives Micron margins to record high amid chip supply constraints
item.description: The chip manufacturer is investing billions to boost capacity in the U.S. and Asia. Executives expect certain chip supplies to remain limited for the foreseeable future.

item.title: 3M, Bain Capital to acquire safety and fire system company for nearly $2B
item.description: The Madison Fire & Rescue acquisition is part of the chemical manufacturer’s and private equity firm’s plans to establish a joint venture.

item.title: NIST director nominee advances despite senators’ MEP concerns
item.description: Arvind Raman was voted out of committee to potentially lead the agency. The administration’s Manufacturing Extension Partnership cuts came up during his confirmation hearing.

item.title: From assessment to automation: 5 steps to smarter manufacturing
item.description: Follow 5 strategic steps to build a smart factory that drives efficiency and maximizes yield.

item.title: Freeze, flee or build: a manufacturer’s playbook for making capital decisions amid uncertainty
item.description: The CapEx queue has never been more complex. Here’s how leading manufacturers decide what to fund.

item.title: Danone to buy protein and fiber food maker Huel
item.description: The Oikos parent is purchasing the powders and ready-to-drink beverage producer for a reported $1.2 billion, enhancing its presence in functional and complete nutrition.

item.title: BlueOval SK delays layoffs at Kentucky battery plant
item.description: Ford recently announced it was dissolving its $11.4 billion EV battery joint venture, its largest manufacturing commitment in the company’s history.

item.title: Elon Musk to build advanced chip factories in Austin, Texas, for SpaceX and Tesla
item.description: The 100 million-square-foot facility will make two kinds of chips for terrestrial and space applications. The Terafab project is reportedly valued at up to $25 billion.

item.title: Inlyte Energy, Ervin Industries ink deal to strengthen US battery storage supply chain
item.description: Inlyte is in the final process of selecting the site of its first U.S. manufacturing facility and anticipates to begin deliveries in 2027.
